note: The closest match to the stated ICP in this batch, and the only one that clears every criterion. The ICP quote names physicians explicitly, and he is one — private practice, hospital work, and newly a professor of medicine, married to another doctor. Income holds at the level the criterion tests: two medical incomes, and he validated the price on its merits rather than resisting it, 'I don't think it's an absurd value... I think actually that is pretty fair.' What blocks him is liquidity timing — an apartment mid-renovation, a second child due in October, a practice restructure, and a USD price that converts to roughly R$25,000-28,000 — not the level of his earnings, so it is recorded as a match with that caveat rather than a miss. Neglected health fits in the precise sense the criterion means: he is in good shape and has let specific pillars slide, in his own words 'I was neglecting a lot of stuff in terms of endurance, in terms of VO2 max.' Good-to-great is his framing exactly, and at 13-14% body fat training four to five times a week he is nowhere near the exclusion. The lesson to carry forward is that the textbook ICP prospect did not close, and he did not close for a reason the ICP does not screen on — currency and life stage — while two prospects well outside it were taken to a handshake in the same week.
